scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hi IT!! The upstairs design floor's 172.16.30.x
machines have STOPPED EXISTING for us downstairs -- from my PC5, 172.16.10.x,
every one of them times out, while my own floor is totally fine!! Something
around the big switch that joins the floors must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone look at it and reconnect me to design -- deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce the outage. From 172.16.10.5 (pc5) I successfully pinged all three design-floor hosts 172.16.30.12/13/14 with 0% loss and sub‑5 ms RTT. Return TTLs of 63 indicate a single routed hop, so inter‑VLAN routing is functioning. On the switching path, the aggregation switch (mswitch0) ports toward switch1 (eth2, VLAN10) and switch3 (eth4, VLAN30) are up and forwarding with no errors or drops. Interface counters on both sides match (switch3 eth0 RX ≈ mswitch0 eth4 TX and vice versa), and ethtool reports 10Gbps full‑duplex, link‑detected. STP shows all relevant ports in forwarding state. VLAN handling is consistent with the site’s design: the access switches (switch1/switch3) tag VLANs using subinterfaces (eth0.10 / eth0.30) bridged to their respective VLAN bridges, and mswitch0 transparently forwards 802.1Q traffic (bridge VLAN table shows untagged/PVID 1 only, which is acceptable for a tag‑transit core bridge).

Localization: No faults observed on mswitch0, switch1, or switch3; pc5 has correct IP and default gateway (172.16.10.254), and routes to 172.16.30.0/24 succeed.

Root cause: No current network fault found; the earlier timeouts were likely transient (host issue, brief churn, or non-network cause) and have cleared.

Corrective fix: None required. Connectivity is restored. If the issue recurs, please note exact time and target IPs and capture a traceroute from pc5; we can then correlate with switch/router logs for any transient events.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms inter‑VLAN routing via pings but does not explicitly state that mswitch0's VLAN 10 and 30 SVIs are up (with their SVI IPs), so it fails the baseline‑SVI check.

The agent reproduced inter‑VLAN traffic (pc5 -> pc12/13/14) and inspected switch/link state; those observations support the 'no anomaly' conclusion. A few specific claims (ethtool speed, perfectly matching counters, explicit SVI addresses) are not fully shown in the log, but the core reachability evidence and interface/bridge state are present and sufficient.
